claim: The Myddosome is a key innate immune signalling platform that forms at the cell surface and contains MyD88 and IRAK proteins which ultimately coordinate the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
source: The Myddosome is a key innate immune signalling platform. It forms at the cell surface and contains MyD88 and IRAK proteins which ultimately coordinate the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as established background information about the Myddosome.

claim: Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) signals via the Myddosome when triggered by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or amyloid-beta (Aβ) aggregates.
source: Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) signals via the Myddosome when triggered by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or amyloid-beta (Aβ) aggregates but the magnitude and time duration of the response are very different for reasons that are unclear.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge and forms the basis for the study.

claim: The magnitude and time duration of TLR4 response are very different for LPS versus Aβ aggregates for reasons that are unclear.
source: Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) signals via the Myddosome when triggered by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or amyloid-beta (Aβ) aggregates but the magnitude and time duration of the response are very different for reasons that are unclear.
evidence: This is stated as the motivation for the study in the abstract.

claim: Myddosomes formed more rapidly after LPS than in response to sonicated Aβ 1–42 fibrils (80 vs 372 s).
source: Myddosomes formed more rapidly after LPS than in response to sonicated Aβ 1–42 fibrils (80 vs 372 s).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The mean lifetimes of the Myddosomes were shorter when triggered by LPS compared to sonicated Aβ fibrils (170 and 220 s), respectively.
source: The mean lifetimes of the Myddosomes were also shorter when triggered by LPS compared to sonicated Aβ fibrils (170 and 220 s), respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: A range of Myddosomes of different sizes (50–500 nm) were formed in both LPS and Aβ triggering cases.
source: In both cases, a range of Myddosome of different sizes (50–500 nm) were formed.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by super-resolution imaging data in Figures 8 and 9.

claim: Small round Myddosomes around 100 nm in size formed at early time points, then reduced in proportion over time.
source: In particular, small round Myddosomes around 100 nm in size formed at early time points, then reduced in proportion over time.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by shape factor analysis in Figure 10.

claim: The multivalency of Aβ fibrils leads to the formation of larger Myddosomes which form more slowly and take longer to disassemble due to their size.
source: Collectively, our data suggest that compared to LPS the multivalency of Aβ fibrils leads to the formation of larger Myddosomes which form more slowly and, due to their size, take longer to disassemble.
evidence: This is the main interpretation of the data presented in the abstract, based on the experimental observations.

claim: Sonicated Aβ fibrils result in less efficient triggering of TLR4 signalling compared to LPS.
source: This explains why sonicated Aβ fibrils results in less efficient triggering of TLR4 signalling and may be a general property of protein aggregates.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and stated in the abstract.

claim: The delayed kinetics and altered structure of Myddosomes may be a general property of protein aggregates.
source: This explains why sonicated Aβ fibrils results in less efficient triggering of TLR4 signalling and may be a general property of protein aggregates.
evidence: This is a speculative generalization based on the findings with Aβ aggregates.

claim: TLR4 activation is important in many diseases including Alzheimer's disease (AD).
source: It is now clear that TLR4 activation is important in many diseases with, for example, its triggering by small aggregates of proteins, such as amyloid-beta (Aβ), thought to be important in the initiation and development of Alzheimer's disease (AD) (Okamura et al., 2001; Reed-Geaghan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: TLR4 triggering by small aggregates of proteins such as amyloid-beta is thought to be important in the initiation and development of Alzheimer's disease.
source: It is now clear that TLR4 activation is important in many diseases with, for example, its triggering by small aggregates of proteins, such as amyloid-beta (Aβ), thought to be important in the initiation and development of Alzheimer's disease (AD) (Okamura et al., 2001; Reed-Geaghan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Two rare genetic variants in the APOE or TREM2 genes are associated with AD and these proteins both can modulate TLR4 signalling.
source: Two rare genetic variants in the APOE or TREM2 genes are associated with AD and these proteins both can modulate TLR4 signalling.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the introduction.

claim: TLR4 priming is required for full activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome which is thought to play an important role in the aetiology of AD.
source: Importantly, TLR4 priming is required for full activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome which is also thought to play an important role in the aetiology of many of AD (Juliana et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Signalling through TLR4 utilises four adaptor proteins: Mal/Tirap, MyD88, Tram, and Trif which form two macromolecular signalling complexes: the Myddosome and the Triffosome.
source: Signalling through TLR4 utilises four adaptor proteins: Myelin and lymphocyte protein (Mal)/(TIR) domain-containing adaptor protein (Tirap), Myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MyD88), Translocating chain-associated membrane protein (Tram), and Toll/interleukin-1 receptor domain-containing adaptor protein inducing interferon beta (Trif) which form two macromolecular signalling complexes: the Myddosome and the Triffosome, respectively (Gay et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The Myddosome consists of MyD88 and IRAK-2 and -4 kinases.
source: The Myddosome consists of MyD88 and IRAK-2 and -4 kinases.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: In a crystal structure of the Myddosome there are six MyD88 molecules, four IRAK4, and four IRAK2 subunits.
source: In a crystal structure of the Myddosome there are six MyD88 molecules, four IRAK4, and four IRAK2 subunits (Lin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Biophysical analysis within cells identifies complexes with six MyD88, but other stoichiometries are present.
source: Our biophysical analysis within cells, also identifies complexes with six MyD88, but other stoichiometries are present (Latty et al., 2018; Moncrieffe et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations to previous work.

claim: Low doses of small Aβ-42 oligomers at concentrations found in the cerebrospinal fluid of AD patients prime TLR4 signalling to induce sustained cytokine production through Myddosome formation.
source: Our previous work shows that low doses of small Aβ-42 oligomers (at concentrations of these proteins found in the cerebrospinal fluid of AD patients) primes TLR4 signalling to induce sustained cytokine production, through Myddosome formation (Hughes et al., 2020), which is a pattern of signalling that is very different to that seen when TLR4 is triggered by LPS.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: The pattern of TLR4 signalling induced by Aβ oligomers is very different to that seen when TLR4 is triggered by LPS.
source: Our previous work shows that low doses of small Aβ-42 oligomers (at concentrations of these proteins found in the cerebrospinal fluid of AD patients) primes TLR4 signalling to induce sustained cytokine production, through Myddosome formation (Hughes et al., 2020), which is a pattern of signalling that is very different to that seen when TLR4 is triggered by LPS.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction based on previous work.

claim: Aβ aggregates are much larger than LPS and potentially multivalent so they could bind multiple TLR4 simultaneously potentially sterically hindering the successful formation of Myddosomes.
source: The Aβ aggregates are much larger than LPS and potentially multivalent so it is possible they could bind multiple TLR4 simultaneously potentially sterically hindering the successful formation of Myddosomes and hence altering the signalling efficiency.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the introduction to explain potential differences in signalling.

claim: Myddosomes assemble within minutes of TLR4 stimulation and contain six MyD88 molecules although larger Myddosomes could form.
source: We found that Myddosomes assemble within minutes of TLR4 stimulation and that they contained six MyD88 molecules although larger Myddosomes could form.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from previous work by the authors.

claim: Lipid partial agonists at TLR4 stimulate slower formation of a smaller number of Myddosomes.
source: Lipid partial agonists at TLR4 stimulate slower formation of a smaller number of Myddosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from previous work.

claim: Only a small number of Myddosomes need to be formed on the cell surface for full cellular signalling to occur.
source: Only a small number of Myddosomes need to be formed on the cell surface for full cellular signalling to occur, and we proposed that the difference between full and partial agonism is determined by Myddosome number, size, and the speed of their formation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding and proposal from previous work.

claim: The difference between full and partial agonism is determined by Myddosome number, size, and the speed of their formation.
source: Only a small number of Myddosomes need to be formed on the cell surface for full cellular signalling to occur, and we proposed that the difference between full and partial agonism is determined by Myddosome number, size, and the speed of their formation.
evidence: This is stated as a proposal from previous work in the introduction.

claim: Small reversible Myddosomes form but signalling requires the formation of stable larger Myddosomes with four or more MyD88.
source: Elegant work using TIRF microscopy supported our hypothesis when studying Myddosome formation in response to triggering of the interleukin 1 receptor in mouse lymphoma cells (Deliz-Aguirre et al., 2021). Here, small reversible Myddosomes formed but signalling required the formation of stable larger Myddosomes with four or more MyD88.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the hypothesis.

claim: TIRF microscopy limits the volume that can be visualised to 200 nm above the coverslip such that only Myddosomes formed on the bottom cell membrane can be seen.
source: This technique limits the volume that can be visualised to 200 nm above the coverslip such that only Myddosomes formed on the bottom cell membrane can be seen so any Myddosomes formed away from this field of view will be lost.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of TIRF microscopy in the introduction.

claim: It is hard to calculate the lifetime of assembled Myddosomes with TIRF because the loss of the Myddosome fluorescence signal could be attributed to either disassembly or trafficking of the complex away from the bottom cell membrane.
source: It is also hard to calculate the lifetime of assembled Myddosomes with TIRF because the loss of the Myddosome fluorescence signal could be attributed to either disassembly or trafficking of the complex away from the bottom cell membrane.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of TIRF microscopy in the introduction.

claim: Confocal microscopy images cells in 3D, but its low imaging speed and out of plane photobleaching means this technique is not capable of repetitive live cell imaging of low-level fluorescence signals.
source: Confocal microscopy images cells in 3D, but its low imaging speed and out of plane photobleaching means this technique is not capable of repetitive live cell imaging of low-level fluorescence signals.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of confocal microscopy in the introduction.

claim: Light sheet 3D scanning can scan the whole-cell sample with relative high speed (single cell scanning only takes 2 s).
source: Light sheet 3D scanning, by scanning the objective or sample stage, can scan the whole-cell sample with relative high speed (single cell scanning only takes 2 s).
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of light sheet microscopy in the introduction.

claim: A nanopipette will accurately deliver individual molecules to a defined position on the cell surface.
source: The use of a nanopipette, will accurately deliver individual molecules to a defined position on the cell surface.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the nanopipette method in the introduction.

claim: ldSPIM uses a nanopipette to control the position from which the molecules are delivered and light sheet microscopy to follow Myddosome formation in live macrophages following TLR4 triggering by LPS or sonicated Aβ fibrils.
source: ldSPIM uses a nanopipette to control the position from which the molecules are delivered and the lightsheet microscopy to follow Myddosome formation in live macrophages following TLR4 triggering by LPS or sonicated Aβ fibrils.
evidence: This is stated as the method developed and used in this study in the introduction.

claim: The majority of sonicated Aβ fibrils were less than 100 nm in length.
source: We firstly characterised the Aβ fibrils using electron microscopy, showing that the majority was less than 100 nm in length (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Sonicated Aβ fibrils showed large population of sub-100 nm oligomers in background of image as well as some larger fibrils.
source: Sonicated sample showed large population of sub-100 nm oligomers in background of image (as well as some larger fibrils).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: PBS and Aβ monomers delivered to macrophages resulted in no triggering.
source: PBS and Aβ monomers were first delivered to macrophages as controls, which resulted in no triggering (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: LPS-triggered Myddosomes started forming within 5 min after local delivery.
source: LPS-triggered Myddosomes started forming within 5 min after local delivery.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on experimental observations.

claim: Myddosomes formed after triggering by sonicated Aβ fibrils first appeared after a significantly longer time, ranging from 200 to 1000s.
source: Myddosomes formed after triggering by sonicated Aβ fibrils first appeared after a significantly longer time, ranging from 200 to 1000s (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4.

claim: On average the LPS-triggered Myddosome first formed at 80 s after delivery and the Aβ-triggered Myddosome first formed at 370 s after delivery.
source: On average the LPS-triggered Myddosome first formed at 80 s after delivery and the Aβ-triggered Myddosome first formed at 370 s after delivery, with LPS stimulation leading to a significantly faster time to first formation than sonicated Aβ fibrils (unpaired two-sided Student's t-test, p = 3.33E−8).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical analysis and shown in Figure 4.

claim: LPS stimulation leads to a significantly faster time to first Myddosome formation than sonicated Aβ fibrils (p = 3.33E−8).
source: On average the LPS-triggered Myddosome first formed at 80 s after delivery and the Aβ-triggered Myddosome first formed at 370 s after delivery, with LPS stimulation leading to a significantly faster time to first formation than sonicated Aβ fibrils (unpaired two-sided Student's t-test, p = 3.33E−8).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical test results.

claim: The lifetime of both LPS and sonicated Aβ fibrils triggered Myddosomes vary significantly and have a large population below 250 s.
source: The lifetime of both LPS and sonicated Aβ fibrils triggered Myddosomes vary significantly and have a large population below 250 s (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Aβ-triggered Myddosomes had a higher proportion of longer lived Myddosomes than LPS.
source: The cumulative lifetimes plot (Figure 5c) shows that Aβ-triggered Myddosomes had a higher proportion of longer lived Myddosomes than LPS.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The difference between the two lifetime distributions (LPS vs Aβ) was significant (Kolmogorov–Smirnov test, p < 0.0001).
source: The difference between the two lifetime distributions was significant (Kolmogorov–Smirnov test, p < 0.0001).
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 5 with statistical test results.

claim: The time taken for the fixed puncta to bleach was much longer compared to the timescales that the Myddosomes were degrading in live cells after stimulation.
source: The time taken for the fixed puncta to bleach was much longer compared to the timescales that the Myddosomes were degrading in live cells after stimulation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 to validate that photobleaching is not a major factor.

claim: Within the first 500 s, there is a 6% loss of detected puncta in fixed cells due to photobleaching.
source: Within the first 500 s, there is a 6% loss of detected puncta; in comparison to the live cell stimulation (Figure 5), there was an approximate 90% drop in the detected puncta for newly assembled puncta within the same time period, suggesting that signal loss during live cell imaging was mostly due to MyD88 puncta degradation rather than photobleaching.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 5—figure supplement 1 with quantitative comparison.

claim: Signal loss during live cell imaging was mostly due to MyD88 puncta degradation rather than photobleaching.
source: Within the first 500 s, there is a 6% loss of detected puncta; in comparison to the live cell stimulation (Figure 5), there was an approximate 90% drop in the detected puncta for newly assembled puncta within the same time period, suggesting that signal loss during live cell imaging was mostly due to MyD88 puncta degradation rather than photobleaching.
evidence: This is stated in the caption of Figure 5—figure supplement 1 based on comparison of fixed and live cell data.

claim: The mean Myddosome lifetimes when triggered by LPS or sonicated Aβ fibrils were 162 and 182 s, respectively.
source: The mean Myddosome lifetimes when triggered by LPS or sonicated Aβ fibrils were 162 and 182 s, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6.

claim: In both LPS- and Aβ-triggered cells, following an initial increase after triggering, the population of membrane localised Myddosomes remained stable, and higher than the number of cytoplasmic Myddosomes.
source: In both LPS- and Aβ-triggered cells, following an initial increase after triggering, the population of membrane localised Myddosomes remained stable, and higher than the number of cytoplasmic Myddosomes, suggesting there most Myddosomes did not undergo internalisation in the first 30 min after stimulation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7.

claim: Most Myddosomes did not undergo internalisation in the first 30 min after stimulation.
source: In both LPS- and Aβ-triggered cells, following an initial increase after triggering, the population of membrane localised Myddosomes remained stable, and higher than the number of cytoplasmic Myddosomes, suggesting there most Myddosomes did not undergo internalisation in the first 30 min after stimulation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The Myddosomes formed by sonicated Aβ fibrils stimulation are larger than those formed by LPS stimulation at all times, especially at early times.
source: The Myddosomes formed by sonicated Aβ fibrils stimulation are larger than those formed by LPS stimulation at all times, especially at early times.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9.

claim: For both LPS and Aβ conditions at 30 min following stimulation, a bimodal distribution of shape factors was observed, consisting of a population of highly circular MyD88 clusters, as well as a more variable population of less circular clusters.
source: We started by measuring the shape factor distributions for LPS and Aβ at an early time point (30 min following stimulation). For both conditions, a bimodal distribution was observed (Figure 10a), consisting of a population of highly circular MyD88 clusters, as well as a more variable population of less circular clusters.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 10a.

claim: The population of clusters with a shape factor close to 1 were mostly very small, with an area below 0.01 µm2 (equivalent to a diameter below approximately 100 nm assuming a perfect circular cluster).
source: By comparing this distribution to the area of the clusters, we observed that this population clusters with a shape factor close to 1 were mostly very small, with an area below 0.01 µm2 (equivalent to a diameter below approximately 100 nm assuming a perfect circular cluster).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 10b.

claim: There was a significant drop in the population of small, circular Myddosomes (shape factor = 1) at later time points after stimulation.
source: Plotting the fraction of clusters with shape factor = 1 compared to all clusters revealed a significant drop in this population at later time points after stimulation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 10d.

claim: At earlier time points (30 min), there was lower populations of small, circular Myddosomes after Aβ triggering compared to LPS triggering.
source: At earlier time points (30 min), there was also lower populations of these smaller, circular Myddosomes after Aβ triggering compared to LPS triggering.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 10d.

claim: LPS-triggered Myddosomes formed faster and are shorter lived than Myddosomes formed by sonicated Aβ fibrils.
source: We observed that LPS-triggered Myddosomes formed faster and are shorter lived than Myddosomes formed by sonicated Aβ fibrils.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of findings in the Discussion section.

claim: In both LPS and Aβ cases, most Myddosomes formed are removed by disassembly at the cell surface.
source: In both cases, most Myddosomes formed are removed by disassembly at the cell surface.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the Discussion section.

claim: The sonicated Aβ fibril is multivalent binding multiple TLR4s and hence forms larger Myddosomes and these Myddosomes would then take longer to form and remove.
source: These differences potentially support our hypothesis that the sonicated Ab fibril is multivalent binding multiple TLR4s and hence forms larger Myddosomes and these Myddosome would then take longer to form and remove.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis supported by the data in the Discussion section.

claim: Viral transduction of MyD88 into cells may result in overexpression of the protein which could lead to structural variation that may be seen under physiological conditions.
source: One limitation of our model is that viral transduction of MyD88 into cells may result in overexpression of the protein which could lead to structural variation that may be seen under physiological conditions.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the Discussion section.

claim: The heterogeneity in Myddosome structure and function may be functionally important.
source: The heterogeneity in Myddosome structure and function, however, may also be functionally important.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation in the Discussion section.

claim: LPS-triggered Myddosome signalling has a negative feedback control system whereby a short MyD88 isoform MyD88s is upregulated.
source: LPS-triggered Myddosome signalling has a negative feedback control system whereby a short MyD88 isoform MyD88s is upregulated.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the Discussion section.

claim: MyD88s lacks the intermediate domain (ID) for IRAK recruitment and thus is signalling incompetent.
source: Myd88s lacks the intermediate domain (ID) for IRAK recruitment and thus is signalling incompetent so this may result in the formation of Myddosomes with different structures at later times.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the Discussion section.

claim: NF-κB translocation to nucleus in response to LPS occurred in the first 30 min after triggering by LPS.
source: In our previous experiments measuring Nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) translocation to nucleus in response to LPS we showed that translocation occurred in the first 30 min after triggering by LPS (Latty et al., 2018), when we observed a high proportion of small Myddosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to previous work.

claim: The small round Myddosomes, formed in higher proportion at early times, are signalling competent.
source: It therefore seems plausible that the small round Myddosomes, formed in higher proportion at early times, are signalling competent.
evidence: This is stated as a plausible inference in the Discussion section.

claim: The larger Myddosomes formed in response to sonicated Aβ fibrils seem to be signalling competent, since prolonged TNFα production over 24 hr was observed following addition of Aβ aggregates.
source: The larger Myddosomes formed in response to sonicated Aβ fibrils also seem to be signalling competent, since we previously observed prolonged TNFα production over 24 hr, following addition of Aβ aggregates (Hughes et al., 2020), during which time we observed mainly larger Myddosomes.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the Discussion section based on previous observations.

claim: The structural diversity observed provides a potential explanation for how diverse signalling outcomes are possible when TLR4 is activated by different agonists.
source: Determining the signalling competency of different sized Myddosomes complexes is an important goal for future studies, but the structural diversity we have observed does provide a potential explanation for how diverse signalling outcomes are possible when TLR4 is activated by different agonists.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation in the Discussion section.

claim: The delay time for Myddosome formation involves dimerisation of TLR4, binding of LPS or Aβ aggregates to the TLR4 dimer followed by Myddosome formation.
source: This delay times involves dimerisation of TLR4, binding of LPS or Aβ aggregates to the TLR4 dimer followed by Myddosome formation.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation of what the delay time represents in the Discussion section.

claim: Preformed TLR4 dimers exist on the cell surface.
source: It is worth noting that in our experiments we deliver the LPS or Aβ aggregates directly onto the surface for 5 s and that we previously showed the presence of the preformed TLR4 dimers on the cell surface (Latty et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to previous work.

claim: LPS has a high affinity for TLR4, estimated to ∼3 nM for lipid A–TLR4-MD-2.
source: The affinity of Aβ aggregates for TLR4 is not known but LPS has a high affinity for TLR4, estimated to ∼3 nM for lipid A–TLR4-MD-2 (Akashi et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: It took 80 s to observe Myddosome formation after LPS delivery, indicating that Myddosome formation is the slow step for LPS triggering.
source: However, even with this high affinity which implies fast binding, direct delivery directly onto the surface and the presence of preformed TLR4 dimers on the cell surface we observed that it took 80 s to observe Myddosome formation. This indicates that Myddosome formation is the slow step for LPS triggering.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the Discussion section based on the experimental observations.

claim: Myddosome formation is likely to be the slow step for Aβ aggregates triggering.
source: This is likely to be the case Aβ aggregates, since pM concentrations of aggregates can trigger TLR4 signalling (Hughes et al., 2020) indicating high affinity.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the Discussion section based on previous work showing high affinity.

claim: pM concentrations of Aβ aggregates can trigger TLR4 signalling indicating high affinity.
source: This is likely to be the case Aβ aggregates, since pM concentrations of aggregates can trigger TLR4 signalling (Hughes et al., 2020) indicating high affinity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to previous work.

claim: There are clear differences between the Myddosomes formed by LPS and Aβ aggregates in their kinetics, size, and shape.
source: Overall, we have found that there are clear differences between the Myddosomes formed by LPS and Aβ aggregates in their kinetics, size, and shape.
evidence: This is stated as a summary conclusion in the Discussion section.

claim: The Myddosomes formed over time also change in size and shape with continual exposure to agonist.
source: Furthermore, the Myddosomes formed over time also change in size and shape with continual exposure to agonist.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the Discussion section.

claim: The lifetime and structure of the Myddosome formed at the cell surface appear to play an important role in the strength of downstream signalling.
source: The lifetime and structure of the Myddosome formed at the cell surface appear to play an important role in the strength of downstream signalling, and the fact that the Myddosomes vary in structure and kinetics may, we speculate, play an important role in explaining how the same cellular components can give rise to multiple different cellular responses.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation and speculation in the Discussion section.

claim: The fact that the Myddosomes vary in structure and kinetics may play an important role in explaining how the same cellular components can give rise to multiple different cellular responses.
source: The lifetime and structure of the Myddosome formed at the cell surface appear to play an important role in the strength of downstream signalling, and the fact that the Myddosomes vary in structure and kinetics may, we speculate, play an important role in explaining how the same cellular components can give rise to multiple different cellular responses.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation in the Discussion section.

claim: The combination of smaller more efficient signalling hubs, which form faster and last for a shorter time may provide a simple explanation for the larger signalling response observed with LPS than with Aβ aggregates.
source: The combination of smaller more efficient signalling hubs, which form faster and last for a shorter time may provide a simple explanation for the larger signalling response observed with LPS than with Aβ aggregates.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation in the Discussion section.

claim: Smaller Aβ aggregates may be expected to be more potent agonists than larger aggregates.
source: If this is correct, then smaller Aβ aggregates may be expected to be more potent agonists than larger aggregates.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction based on the findings in the Discussion section.

claim: The reduced rate of Myddosome formation, longer lifetime and altered Myddosome structure may contribute to the weaker response from sonicated Aβ fibrils.
source: Furthermore, it suggests the reduced rate of Myddosome formation, longer lifetime and altered Myddosome structure may contribute to the weaker response from sonicated Aβ fibrils.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation in the Discussion section.

claim: Larger multivalent protein aggregates in general may trigger TLR4 signalling less effectively than LPS giving rise to the low levels of chronic inflammation observed in neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Given the common aggregation pathway and similar aggregate structure of other aggregation prone proteins, such as tau and a-synuclein, larger multivalent protein aggregates in general may trigger TLR4 signalling less effectively than LPS giving rise to the low levels of chronic inflammation observed in neurodegenerative diseases.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation and generalization in the Discussion section.
